annotation_description: Played Hallowed Fountain paying 2 life when Island would have provided the same U mana untapped for free. The 2 life was wasted since Island enables Spell Snare equally well on turn 1, and future turns work out the same (Floodfarm Verge activates off Island too).

With 3 mana available (Forest, Ba Sing Se, Llanowar Elves), the player could cast Badgermole Cub (1G) which is a 2/2 that also earthbends a land into a creature with a +1/+1 counter, creating significantly more board presence. Instead they cast a second Llanowar Elves, which only adds a 1/1 body and mana acceleration. While ramping toward Mightform Harmonizer is reasonable, Badgermole Cub develops a much stronger board (2/2 + a 1/1 land creature) and the Cub's ability to generate extra mana from creature taps also provides acceleration. Additionally, playing into an opponent with Spell Snare mana open (UU available) is risky since Llanowar Elves costs 1 (not 2), but Badgermole Cub costs 2 and could be Spell Snared. However, they could also play Temple Garden first for an additional land, then have even more options. The sequencing of land drop before spell is also a consideration - they should play Temple Garden first regardless of which creature they cast.

message: Choose which mana to produce from Floodfarm Verge (tapping to pay for a spell)
chosen_display: 2. {T}: Add {U}. Activate only if you control a Plains or an Island.
annotation_description: Using No More Lies (a premium 2-mana counterspell) to counter a second Llanowar Elves when holding Day of Judgment to handle creatures and Spell Snare for 2-drops. No More Lies would be better saved for a high-impact spell like Mightform Harmonizer or another threat that Day of Judgment can't answer.

The opponent has 3 untapped lands (Hallowed Fountain, Floodfarm Verge, Island) which is exactly enough mana to cast No More Lies (WU + 3 to pay is irrelevant - they can counter it). While No More Lies is already in the graveyard, the opponent could have other counterspells. More importantly, casting Mightform Harmonizer via Warp ({2}{G}) means it gets exiled at the next end step, making it a temporary threat. Meanwhile, the opponent likely has interaction ready with 3 open mana. Seam Rip (W) could have been cast first to exile a potential blocker or problematic permanent, and it's a permanent that sticks around. However, the bigger issue is that casting a Warp creature into open mana when the opponent is playing a UW control deck with counterspells is risky - if countered, you lose the card entirely (and with No More Lies-style effects, it gets exiled). The Warp version already exiles itself at end step, so the upside is just one combat step with landfall trigger doublings. Playing Seam Rip first (there are no valid targets with mana value 2 or less on opponent's board though - only lands) means Seam Rip actually has no valid targets here. So the real question is whether to cast Mightform Harmonizer via Warp into 3 open mana from a UW control opponent. Given the opponent already used No More Lies (it's in the graveyard), they might have Spell Snare (which hits MV 2, not MV 3 Warp cost). The risk is moderate but the line is reasonable to apply pressure. Actually, looking more carefully - the Warp cost is {2}{G} (MV 3), and the opponent has exactly the mana for counterspells like another No More Lies or similar. But the Harmonizer is being warped, meaning if it resolves, it provides a huge damage burst with landfall triggers doubling power. This is a tempo play that could be punished but also could be game-winning. This seems more questionable than a clear blunder.

message: Choose spell or ability to play: Ba Sing Se
chosen_display: 2. {2}{G}, {T}: Earthbend 2. Activate only as a sorcery. (Target land you control becomes a 0/0 creature with haste that's still a land. Put two +1/+1 counters on it. When it dies or is exiled, return it to the battlefield tapped.)
annotation_description: Activating Ba Sing Se's earthbend 2 for 4 mana (3 mana + tap) when the opponent is completely tapped out leaves only 1 mana remaining, preventing deployment of the full hand. Deploying all three hand cards (Badgermole Cub + Sazh's Chocobo + Seam Rip for ~4 mana total) would put more bodies on board and still get earthbend 1 from Badgermole Cub's ETB trigger, maximizing the pressure window while the opponent can't interact.

Failed to cast Sazh's Chocobo for {G} with one untapped Ba Sing Se available while opponent is completely tapped out. After a board wipe, deploying a creature with landfall synergy to start rebuilding is important, especially when the opponent can't interact.

The opponent has zero creatures on the battlefield — all their creatures are in exile. Day of Judgment would currently destroy nothing. Meanwhile, Jeskai Revelation is an extremely powerful card that bounces a permanent, deals 4 damage, creates tokens, draws 2 cards, and gains 4 life — all crucial when at 10 life needing to turn the corner with The Unagi of Kyoshi Island in hand.

Playing Forest before casting Felidar Retreat means the landfall trigger from Forest won't trigger Felidar Retreat (since it's not on the battlefield yet). This wastes a landfall trigger that would have created a 2/2 Cat Beast token or pumped all creatures.

annotation_description: At 7 opponent life with no blockers, casting Mightform Harmonizer with Warp ({2}{G}) would create a 4/4 hasty attacker dealing 4 damage (opponent to 3), putting them in lethal range next turn. Instead, earthbend 2 creates only a 2/2 attacker dealing 2 damage (opponent to 5), which is less pressure despite the creature persisting.

Grk41F Drama chose not to attack with Mightform Harmonizer (4/4) into an empty board when the opponent is at 7 life. Attacking would put the opponent to 3 life, making lethal trivially easy next turn. The opponent has no blockers, so there is zero risk in attacking.
